harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured a persistent UFW host firewall on node1 (Ubuntu 16.04) that allows inbound SSH (22/tcp) and TCP 8080, and rejects all other unrelated inbound connections by default. Verified persistence across a full node restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS and existing firewall tooling (ufw present but inactive)
Set UFW default policies: deny/reject incoming, allow outgoing
Allowed 22/tcp (SSH) and 8080/tcp explicitly (both IPv4 and IPv6)
Enabled ufw persistently (systemctl enabled, survives reboot) and confirmed active status with correct rule set
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, ufw status, sshd status
Issued a single safe reboot (shutdown -r now) on node1, acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec access returned; confirmed boot_id changed, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified post-restart that ufw is active with identical allow rules for 22/tcp and 8080/tcp, default reject incoming, and sshd active

evidence.requirement: Persistent firewall permits SSH and TCP 8080, rejects other inbound
evidence.summary: ufw configured with default reject incoming / allow outgoing, explicit allow rules for 22/tcp and 8080/tcp (v4+v6), enabled at boot; iptables INPUT chain confirms DROP policy backing the ufw reject chain
Captured boot_id 8336c3a1-91fc-4135-b26a-5d2863cb2594, ufw active with correct rules, sshd active before reboot
shutdown -r now issued in background; command returned 'reboot-issued' immediately

evidence.requirement: Node becomes unreachable then recovers with changed boot identity
evidence.summary: First poll refused (node down mid-reboot); second poll returned new boot_id f333f02f-04b7-481d-8994-5458cfb65bb3, proving an actual restart

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of firewall persistence and required services
evidence.summary: After reboot, ufw automatically active again (enabled service) with identical rules (22/tcp, 8080/tcp allowed, default reject incoming) and sshd active, confirming the firewall configuration survived the restart
